dedupe_keys.name: taiwan cost benefit analysis of composting biogas power and biomass fuel from agricultural wastes 2018

description: This case study compares the cost-effectiveness of three ways of recycling agricultural waste in Taiwan to guide business investment and government policy. Esher Hsu of National Taipei University published it in Waste Management in 2021. The three routes, chosen from the regulations and policy support for agricultural waste in Taiwan, are composting, biogas power generation and biomass fuel. The analysis uses primary data from sampling surveys carried out in 2018, supplemented by national statistics. The article is available online by subscription, and the abstract is free on PubMed. Coverage is national. Caveats: results reflect 2018 prices and feed-in tariffs, and the survey data are not published. All three routes were profitable in 2018, with benefit to cost ratios above one and positive net present values; cost-effectiveness varied with route, input mix and scale. Mixing chicken manure with other wastes for compost and making biomass fuel rods from rice straw were the most cost-effective, small livestock farms recovered biogas energy inefficiently, and biogas power depended heavily on feed-in tariffs. The author recommends co-processing centres and differentiated feed-in tariffs. Simulation uses: costs and returns of agricultural waste recycling routes for rural waste and bioenergy planning models. Related records: the Taiwan industrial waste reporting statistics (data-moenv-taiwan-industrial-waste-reporting-statistics) cover another Taiwanese waste stream.
